Can optimism survive truth? Command the FRV Aurora in an episodic sci-fi visual novel where your choices shape the crew, and the truth. On Steam and iOS.
An episodic sci-fi visual novel. Your choices shape the crew, and the truth.
Windows · macOS · Linux · free demo on Steam
Free demo on itch.io · Windows · no Steam account needed
The frontier is not what it seems

You are the Commander of the FRV Aurora, a Frontier Response Vessel dispatched to investigate incidents on humanity's expanding edge. The United Earth Alliance has built a utopia: 150 years of peace, cooperation, and exploration.
But something is wrong on the frontier. And the more you investigate, the less certain anything becomes.
Four specialists, four perspectives. Every decision shapes your relationships with Kira, Marcus, Amara, and Jax, and what they'll trust you with.
Investigate impossible phenomena in humanity's optimistic future. Each case challenges what's supposed to exist at all.
Each episode is a complete investigation that builds toward something larger. Play one at a time, or binge the whole season.
Every character brought to life with full voice acting and an original atmospheric soundtrack.
Your philosophy matters. The ending you reach reflects not just your choices, but your worldview.
24 episodes planned. Built by one person who wanted to play this game and couldn't find it.

Need help with The Aurora Chronicles? Report a bug, ask about saves and progress, request your data, or contact Entropy about press. Every email gets a reply.
Support
We read everything. We answer the rest.
How can we help?
The Aurora Chronicles is built by one person at Entropy. There's no support ticket queue and no bot on the other end — just email. Reach out about any of the below and you'll get a real reply.
Bugs & crashes
Something broke, soft-locked, or won't launch? Tell us your platform (Steam, iOS, Android), the episode, and what happened. Screenshots and logs help a lot.
Saves & progress

Your progress is saved locally on your device, and on Steam it also syncs to Steam Cloud. We don't keep copies on our servers, so a deleted or corrupted local save usually can't be restored — but if a save won't load when it should, that's a bug, and we'd like to hear about it.
Your data & privacy
Request a copy or deletion of the data associated with your anonymous player identifier. See the Privacy Policy for what we store and your rights.
Press & business
Press kits, review keys, curator requests, and partnership inquiries are all welcome at the same address below.
Contact
To cut down on spam, the email address is revealed after a quick human check.

privacy.find: Privacy Policy — The Aurora Chronicles
Privacy Policy for The Aurora Chronicles by Entropy: what anonymous data the game collects, what it doesn't, and how to request a copy or deletion of your data.
Privacy Policy
The Aurora Chronicles — by Entropy
Effective date: February 14, 2026 · Last updated: June 11, 2026
1. Who We Are

The Aurora Chronicles is developed and published by Kitti Vongsay (known online as kittikun), a sole proprietor (個人事業主) based in Tokyo, Japan, operating under the trade name Entropy. This policy applies to The Aurora Chronicles on all platforms, including Steam, iOS, and Android.
2. What Data We Collect
We collect only what is necessary to provide the game experience:
Save Data: Your game progress is stored locally on your device. On Steam, save data is also synced via Steam Cloud. We do not currently store saves on our own servers.

Choice Statistics: When you make in-game choices, your selections are recorded to show community statistics (e.g., what percentage of players chose each option). Choices are linked to an anonymous identifier automatically generated by Firebase on your device. This data is stored on Supabase (cloud database). Other players only see aggregated percentages (e.g., “65% of players chose option A”), never individual choices.

Purchases (mobile only): On iOS and Android, in-app purchases are processed by Apple and Google. We use RevenueCat to manage purchase entitlements; RevenueCat receives an app-generated user identifier, your purchase and transaction history, and basic device information so we can unlock the content you bought and restore it across reinstalls. We never receive or store your payment card details.

Analytics & Crash Reports: We collect anonymous gameplay analytics to improve game quality, identify bugs, and understand how players engage with content. This data may include session duration, device information (OS, language, screen resolution), app version, and in-game events such as episode progress and menu interactions. Analytics and crash/performance diagnostics are processed by Unity Technologies (Unity Gaming Services) on all platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android). On mobile (iOS, Android), gameplay analytics are additionally processed by Google (Google Analytics for Firebase), and crash reports — including device type, OS version, and crash logs — by Firebase Crashlytics. We do not intentionally collect personally identifiable information through analytics, and we do not link analytics data to individual user accounts.

Push Notifications (mobile only): If you opt in to release notifications (for example, by tapping “Notify me when the next episode releases”), Firebase Cloud Messaging generates a device registration token so we can send you a notification when a new episode becomes available. Notifications are delivered as broadcasts grouped by language, and the token is used solely to deliver these messages — it is not used to identify you. You can turn notifications off at any time in your device settings or in the in-game Settings menu. Push notifications are not used on desktop (Steam) platforms.

The game does not require an account. Your save data stays local to your device (or synced via Steam Cloud on Steam). Choice statistics are recorded using an anonymous Firebase identifier, which cannot be used to identify you personally.
3. What We Do NOT Collect
We do not store or use IP addresses or location data for tracking purposes.
Analytics across all platforms are limited to anonymous, aggregated data (see Section 2). We do not use analytics to identify or track individual players.
We do not serve advertisements.
We do not sell your personal data, and we do not share personal data for advertising purposes. We share data only with the service providers necessary to operate the game, as described in Section 4.
4. Third-Party Services
The following third-party services may process data on our behalf:

Firebase (Google): Provides anonymous authentication (Firebase Authentication) used to key your choice statistics, and delivers optional episode-release push notifications on mobile (Firebase Cloud Messaging). Subject to Google's Privacy Policy.
Supabase: Stores choice statistics data linked to your anonymous Firebase identifier. Subject to Supabase's Privacy Policy.

Unity Gaming Services (Unity Technologies): Collects anonymous gameplay analytics and diagnostics (crash and performance data) on all platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android). Subject to Unity's Privacy Policy.
Google Analytics for Firebase & Firebase Crashlytics: Collects anonymous usage data and crash data on mobile (iOS and Android) to help us improve the game. Subject to Google's Privacy Policy.
Steam (Valve): Handles platform accounts, purchases, and Steam Cloud save sync. Subject to Steam's Privacy Policy.
Apple: Handles App Store purchases and accounts on iOS. Subject to Apple's Privacy Policy.
Google Play: Handles purchases and accounts on Android. Subject to Google's Privacy Policy.

RevenueCat: Manages in-app purchase entitlements on mobile (iOS and Android). Receives an app-generated user identifier, purchase and transaction history, and device information to unlock and restore purchased content. Subject to RevenueCat's Privacy Policy.
We do not have access to your payment information on any platform.
5. Analytics Data Retention

Anonymous analytics data is retained according to each provider's standard retention policies: Unity Gaming Services retains data for up to 12 months, and Google Analytics retains data for up to 14 months. These periods may be adjusted in their respective dashboards. We do not use analytics to identify individual players.
6. Data Storage & Security

Choice statistics are stored on Supabase. Anonymous authentication is handled by Firebase (Google Cloud). We use industry-standard security measures to protect your data. However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure.

Some of our service providers (Firebase, Supabase) operate servers outside Japan, including in the United States. By using the game, you consent to your data being transferred to and processed in these jurisdictions, subject to those providers' applicable data transfer safeguards.
7. Children's Privacy

The Aurora Chronicles is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13. If you believe a child has provided us with personal data, please contact us and we will delete it promptly.
8. Your Rights
You may at any time:
Request a copy of any personal data we hold about you
Request deletion of the choice-statistics data associated with your anonymous identifier
Play without an account — the game requires none, and saves stay local (or on Steam Cloud)
To make a request, contact us using the details in Section 10 below.
9. Changes to This Policy
We may update this policy from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated effective date. Continued use of the game after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
10. Contact
For privacy requests or any other questions, please reach us through our support page:

cookies.find: Website Privacy & Cookies — The Aurora Chronicles
How the entropy.kittikun.jp website uses Google Analytics, cookies, and embedded video, how we ask consent by region, and how to control or decline them.
Website Privacy & Cookies
entropy.kittikun.jp — by Entropy
Effective date: June 4, 2026
1. What This Page Covers

This notice explains how the entropy.kittikun.jp website handles analytics and cookies. It is separate from the game's Privacy Policy, which covers data collected inside The Aurora Chronicles on Steam, iOS, and Android.
2. Analytics We Use

We use Google Analytics 4 to understand how many people visit this website and where they come from — for example, total visits, which pages are viewed, the referring site or search, and approximate location (country or region). This helps us see which announcements and channels are reaching people.
We use this only in aggregate. We do not build advertising profiles, we do not show ads, and we do not sell or share this data for advertising. Ad-related and personalization signals are disabled.
3. Cookies

When analytics is active, Google Analytics sets first-party cookies (named _ga and _ga_<id>) containing a randomly generated identifier used to distinguish returning from new visits. These cookies do not contain your name, email, or anything you type. They expire automatically (up to about two years) and can be cleared at any time in your browser.
No analytics cookies are set until analytics is active (see Section 4). Google Analytics 4 does not store your raw IP address.
4. Your Consent & How to Change It

If you visit from the EU, EEA, the UK, or Switzerland, analytics stays switched off until you choose “Accept” on the cookie banner. If you decline, no analytics cookies are set and the site works normally. Visitors from other regions have analytics enabled by default, as permitted by local law.
You can change your choice at any time:
Review my cookie choice
You can also clear this site's cookies and site data in your browser, which resets the banner.
5. Embedded Video

Episode trailers are embedded from YouTube using the privacy-enhanced youtube-nocookie.com mode. The player loads with the page rather than waiting for a click, so your browser contacts YouTube (Google) when the trailers come into view — but in this mode YouTube sets no cookies until you actually play a video. Once you play, YouTube may set its own cookies; that playback is governed by Google's Privacy Policy.
6. Where Data Goes

Website analytics is processed by Google (Google Analytics). Data may be transferred to and processed on Google's servers outside Japan and the EEA, including in the United States, subject to Google's applicable data-transfer safeguards. Google Analytics data is retained for up to 14 months.
7. Contact
For any question about this notice, reach us through our support page:
